legend: C3 glomerulonephritis associated with monoclonal gammopathy. The glomerulus exhibits a membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis pattern of injury, with global mesangial expansion by an increase in mesangial cell number and abundant silver-negative glassy immune deposits, together with segmental duplication of the glomerular basement membrane (JMS stain) (<<33507>>). On immunofluorescence, there is bright granular global glomerular staining for C3 (<<33508>>). Glomeruli were negative for IgG, IgA, kappa, and lambda (not shown). An electron microscopy image showing mesangial electron-dense deposits (short arrows) as well as a hump-shaped subepithelial deposit at the mesangial waist (long arrow) (<<33509>>).

Chronic glomerular microangiopathy associated with monoclonal gammopathy. A high-power light microscopy image showing glomerular basement membrane thickening and segmental narrow duplication (arrows) (PAS) (<<33512>>). An electron microscopy image showing glomerular basement membrane duplication, cellular interposition and widening of the subendothelial zone by electron-lucent fluffy-appearing material. No electron-dense deposits were seen, and immunofluorescence was negative (<<33513>>).

Light chain proximal tubulopathy. Proximal tubular cells are variably extended by numerous light-blue inclusions (trichrome stain) (<<33518>>). A high-power electron microscopy image of a proximal tubular cell shows intracytoplasmic crystalline inclusions with variable shapes (rhomboidal, polygonal, rod-shaped); the majority of crystals appear to lie free within the cytosol (<<33519>>). Immunofluorescence performed on Pronase-digested, paraffin-embedded tissue shows proximal tubular intracytoplasmic crystals staining positive for kappa light chain I (<<33520>>) with negative staining for lambda light chain (<<33521>>).

Proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal immunoglobulin deposits. The membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis pattern of injury is characterized by global mesangial hypercellularity and sclerosis, widespread duplication of the glomerular basement membrane, and segmental cellular interposition; infiltrating inflammatory cells are also present (PAS) (<<33522>>). The endocapillary proliferative glomerulonephritis pattern is characterized by global endocapillary hypercellularity and abundant intracapillary infiltrating inflammatory cells, without glomerular basement membrane duplication (PAS) (<<33523>>). On electron microscopy, large subendothelial electron-dense deposits (arrows) are seen (<<33524>>). A high-power electron microscopy image showing granular intramembranous electron-dense deposits without substructure (<<33525>>). Immunofluorescence images in proliferative glomerulonephritis with monoclonal IgG deposits showing glomerular positivity for IgG (<<33526>>), IgG3 subclass (<<33527>>), and kappa light chain (<<33528>>), with negative staining for lambda light chain (<<33529>>). Glomeruli were negative for IgA, IgM, IgG1, IgG2, and IgG4 (not shown).

Immunotactoid glomerulopathy. The membranoproliferative glomerulonephritis pattern of immunotactoid glomerulopathy is characterized by increased lobulation, global mesangial hypercellularity and sclerosis, and duplication of the glomerular basement membranes with segmental cellular interposition; intracapillary infiltrating inflammatory cells are present (JMS) (<<33553>>). The membranous pattern of immunotactoid glomerulopathy is characterized by global glomerular basement membrane thickening with vacuolization, without endocapillary hypercellularity or glomerular basement membrane duplication (PAS) (<<33554>>). On electron microscopy, the glomerular deposits are composed of long straight microtubules with parallel alignment (<<33555>>). Immunofluorescence images in a case of the monoclonal variant of immunotactoid glomerulopathy show granular global mesangial and glomerular basement membrane staining for IgG (<<33556>>) and lambda light chain (<<33557>>), and negative staining for kappa light chain (<<33558>>).
